facts.text: Goshen was founded in 1799 by German and English settlers, including Jacob Myers, who migrated from western Pennsylvania after the Revolutionary War.
The town sits beside the Little Miami River, a National Wild and Scenic River, and its East Fork, offering scenic waterways that shape local life.
One of Clermont County’s oldest structures, the Cook Log Cabin was built in 1803 and now serves as a preserved historic site in Goshen.
The Goshen Township Historical Society runs the 1843 OH-28 museum, where visitors can explore local history and the library.
Goshen hosts a public library that is a branch of the Clermont County Public Library system, providing community resources.
In 2026, the town celebrated America’s 250th birthday with a commemorative flag produced by the historical society.
